RATIONALE:
Q1: The test the questions name, `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py::test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command` (line 228), runs in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, in the "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests" step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 879-882). That step comes after "PR body auto-close lint unit tests", which matches the triage's most likely cause. On main, the test's `_closed_pipe_diagnostics` docstring (lines 249-250) already records that ubuntu-26.04 runners resend output through Rust coreutils and the test sees `rc=0`. So the failure comes from the runner image and the base branch, not from PR #9268. The GITHUB FACTS show PR #9246 is open and unmerged with the title "Fix the last two CI failures on ubuntu-26.04 runners (heartbeat clock, closed-reader test)", which is exactly this failure. Option A can't be carried out here: working out what #9246 leaves out needs its diff, which is not in the checkout, and the pipeline cannot close issues. Under the data-provision guard and the pipeline-capability rule, C is the conservative fallback that leaves the work to #9246. It also avoids two branches editing the same `gh_retry`/test code, which risks merge conflicts.
Q2: This answer only applies if code ends up changing here, for example if #9246 closes without merging. In that case, fix the root cause in the production helper. `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` `gh_retry` lines 1228-1231 copy `stdout_file` back to the caller's stdout with `cat "${stdout_file}" || _gh_retry_replay_rc=$?`. The header comment at lines 1196-1198 promises that undelivered output from a successful attempt gives a non-zero status. On a `cat` that exits 0 when the reader has closed the pipe, that promise breaks, and callers get `rc=0` for output that never arrived. Loosening the test (B, or the test part of C) would only hide that, so keep the test's assertion unchanged.
